decisions.question: Where do observed streams go, now that observe is rebuilt whole (the bus's own first-value microtask with the deliveries made before it, the forwarding subscription of D5, the bootstrap hold and step 2 of start(), the conversion as an error event) and nidana.runtime.6 (registry, cells, observe) would come to about 700 lines?

options.label: keep observe in nidana.runtime.6
options.consequence: no new phase and no new edge, but .6 spans about two review windows (~700 lines), against the PE rule

options.label: append nidana.runtime.15 between .7 and .8
options.consequence: two phases of ~360 and ~350 lines; .15 tests against the real start() and lands step 2 itself; new edges .2/.6/.7 -> .15 and .15 -> .8; .6 renamed Registry and cells; bus-api@v2 produced_by gains .15

options.label: append nidana.runtime.15 between .6 and .7
options.consequence: same split, .7 composes steps 2 and 3, but .15 must test the after-start path through a seam (start() lands later) and .7 gains an edge on .15

decisions.why: The skill's sizing rule says a phase that cannot fit one review window is split. The stand-ins show observe growing from about 45 to about 180 lines of code (forwarding subscription, own first values, hold), so .6 cannot hold it with the cells. Cutting along the cells/subscriptions seam (D2) gives two sizes inside the window. Placing .15 after .7 lets it use the real start() and land step 2 with the mechanism it connects, as .12 lands step 1; .8 is the first phase whose replay subscribes, so it gains the edge. The record says append 'only work no existing phase owns': the rebuilt observe is new work (its v1 form on RxDart subjects is gone), which is how I read it; flagged in notes. Signal that would change my mind: a first implementation showing observe at well under 200 lines with tests.

decisions.question: Where do the write-chain rule (topology-dsl@v2 G26, Live interpretation 7) and G23's plan comparison go, given .9 would reach about 530 lines with the chains and .11 about 550 with the comparison?

options.label: chains in .9, comparison in .11
options.consequence: no new phase, two phases well over the window

options.label: append nidana.runtime.16 after .10 and before .11
options.consequence: one phase holds the pure chain membership, the comparison, the chain's end over synchronous and time-dependent stages, and reduceInto (moved from .9); new edges .10 -> .16, .16 -> .11; the lanes also meet at .11

options.label: append nidana.runtime.16 between .9 and .10
options.consequence: chains over synchronous stages in .16, .10 cancels time-stage resources at a chain's end; .11 waits on .9 and .16 only; the chain rule reviewed in two phases; three new edges

options.label: a pure phase for chain membership and the comparison
options.consequence: ~230 lines of pure code, but the remaining effects (~175 lines) fall below the floor or overfill .9 and .10

decisions.why: Both pieces are functions over a plan's stages and their inputs (the stand-in shares one stage-inputs visitor); on the stand-ins they are about 90 and 110 of the interpreter's 200 added lines. One phase after .10 reviews the chain rule whole, every stage kind included, with the fewest new edges. The comparison must precede .11, whose checks-only G23 case (plans differing in a seed or closure) replays there. The pure functions sit in an effect phase because they read nidana.model.9's stage classes and visitors, which the pure band (nidana.model.8 only) cannot wait on without delaying .5; they are unit-tested first within .16. Signal: if .11 had room (it does not, ~400 after G42 and the held activations), the comparison would go there.

decisions.question: What does the pure connection-order function take: TopologyDefinition values or the TopicRef sets they read and write?

options.label: TopologyDefinition values
options.consequence: .4 would consume topology-ir@v1 and wait on nidana.model.10, which delivers TopologyDefinition's computed reads and writes; topology-ir@v1's consumers gain nidana.runtime.4

options.label: TopicRef sets per activation
options.consequence: the pure band stays on topic-model@v1 and nidana.model.8; .12 passes each definition's reads and writes

decisions.why: TopologyDefinition is a factory whose reads and writes are computed (topology-ir@v1 Delivery: nidana.model.10). Taking the sets keeps the pure band's single model edge and adds no contract edge. D3 says 'a pure function over the reads and writes of the TopologyDefinition values', which this satisfies.

decisions.question: D8 restated: where do start()'s three steps land?

options.label: step 3 at .7, step 2 at .15, step 1 at .12
options.consequence: each step with the slice it reaches; the 90 + 28 cases that call start() replay from .7/.8 on

options.label: start() whole at .12
options.consequence: holds every case that calls start() back until .12 for the one step that needs wiring

options.label: lifecycle slice whole at .14
options.consequence: no delivery guarantee replays before the last phase

decisions.chosen: step 3 at .7, step 2 at .15, step 1 at .12
decisions.why: bus-api@v2 G34 gives start() three steps; step 1 needs activation wiring, so the first D8 ('start() lands with the publish path') no longer holds. Recounted on the v2 fixtures: 90 of 109 bus-api cases and 28 of 50 bus-testing cases call start(). A case that needs step 1 activates before start() and one that needs step 2 observes before it, so neither replays earlier anyway.

decisions.question: Is the bus running during start(), so that work start() runs (a subscriber's or observer's callback) may activate a MODULE or PAGE topology, acquire a module, or subscribe as after start()? bus-api@v2 and Spec §3.13 say the bus is bootstrapping 'until start()' and do not say what a call made during its steps is.

options.label: running from the moment start() begins
options.consequence: a callback in step 3 (an executor pushing a page on the deep link) can activate the page topology and acquire modules; a subscription it makes gets the after-start first-value microtask; a nested start() does nothing; removeTopic from that work throws as during a delivery

options.label: running only once step 3 returns
options.consequence: a callback during start() could not activate MODULE or PAGE topologies (G42) and a subscription it made would be held for a start() already under way, never connected

options.label: running after step 1
options.consequence: inconsistent: step 2 callbacks see running while step 1 observers see bootstrapping

decisions.chosen: running from the moment start() begins
decisions.why: The stand-ins that pass every suite (bus-api-v2 v2, runtime-topic-storage owned) flip lifecycle first; the alternative strands subscriptions made during start(). A consumer relies on the answer (navigation executor, flutter module acquire on the bootstrap deep link), so it is emitted as a compatible amend of bus-api@v2. The Specification is silent on calls made during start(), so the point is marked for upstreaming.
